User Story: As a user in a fresh repo, I want to start tracking stacks so I can build diffs.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Detects trunk (origin/HEAD -> current branch -> 'main'), writes state, prints 'initialized stacked (trunk: X)' then 'next: st create <name>'. Exit 0.

User Story: As a user, I want to pick the trunk explicitly via --trunk.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st init --trunk <name>' uses that branch as trunk if it exists; errors 'trunk branch X does not exist' otherwise.

User Story: As a user re-running init, I want a clear no-op instead of an error.
Expected Behaviour (from code): If already initialized, prints 'stacked already initialized (trunk: X)' with alreadyInitialized=true, exit 0.

User Story: As a user outside a git repo, I want a clear error.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st init' outside a git repo errors 'not inside a git repository: ...', exit 1.

User Story: As a user, I want to create a new branch stacked on the current one.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Creates branch, tracks it with parent=current, prints 'Created X on top of Y', Branch=X. Exit 0.
Errors Found: F3: "st create <invalid-name>" leaks raw multi-line git error + hints (git checkout -b ...: fatal: not a valid branch name ...) instead of a friendly message. Validate the name up front.
Fix Applied: git.CheckBranchName (git check-ref-format) validates the name in runCreate up front; emits "X is not a valid branch name" instead of git's raw fatal+hints.

User Story: As a user, I want to stage+commit and create in one step with -a -m.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st create X -a -m msg' stages all, commits on new branch, tracks it.

User Story: As a user, I want a clear error if I pass -m with nothing staged.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st create X -m msg' with clean tree errors 'no staged changes to commit; stage changes or pass -a'.

User Story: As a user, I want a clear error if I have staged changes but no -m.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st create X' with staged changes errors 'staged changes present; provide a commit message with -m'.

User Story: As a user, I want creation to refuse an existing branch name.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st create X' where X exists errors 'branch X already exists'.

User Story: As a user on an untracked branch, I want creation refused.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Current branch not trunk and not tracked errors 'current branch X is not the trunk or a tracked branch'.

User Story: As a user, I want -a without -m rejected.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st create X -a' errors '-a requires a commit message (-m <msg>)'.

User Story: As a user, I want a usage error if I omit the name.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st create' errors 'create requires exactly one branch name' and prints usage.

User Story: As a user, I want to amend the current branch and auto-restack descendants.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Bare 'st modify' stages all tracked (-a default true), amends tip (no edit), restacks upstack, prints 'Amended X' + restacked list.

User Story: As a user, I want to amend with a new message.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st modify -m msg' amends commit message, restacks descendants, prints 'Amended X with new message'.

User Story: As a user, I want to add a brand-new commit with --commit.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st modify --commit -m msg' creates a new commit (not amend), restacks descendants, prints 'Committed on X'.

User Story: As a user, I want --commit without -m rejected.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st modify --commit' errors '--commit requires a commit message (-m <msg>)'.

User Story: As a user, I want modify refused on the trunk.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st modify' on trunk errors 'refusing to modify the trunk branch X'.

User Story: As a user, I want modify refused on an untracked branch.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Errors 'branch X is not tracked'.

User Story: As a user with descendants and unstaged changes (-a=false), I want a dirty-tree guard.
Expected Behaviour (from code): With descendants and unstaged changes and -a=false, returns ErrDirty (exit 4).

User Story: As a user, I want to rebase my branch and everything above onto current parents.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st restack' from a branch rebases it + upstack; prints 'restacked' + names, or 'everything up to date'.

User Story: As a user on the trunk, I want to restack every tracked branch.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st restack' on trunk restacks all branches (parents before children).

User Story: As a user, I want to preview a restack with --dry-run.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st restack --dry-run' prints 'would restack' list, DryRun=true, mutates nothing.

User Story: As a user, I want restack refused on a dirty tree.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Dirty working tree returns ErrDirty (exit 4).

User Story: As a user hitting a conflict, I want a clear recovery path.
Expected Behaviour (from code): A rebase conflict returns ErrConflict (exit 2) naming branch+onto, pointing to 'st continue'/'st abort'; leaves git rebase in progress.

User Story: As a user, I want to see my stack as a tree with trunk at the bottom.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st log' prints forest deepest-first; current branch marked with green bold marker; '(needs restack)' on drift; tip subject dimmed.

User Story: As a user/agent, I want the stack as machine-readable JSON.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st log --json' prints nested tree from trunk with name/parent/parentSHA/current/needsRestack/topCommit/children.

User Story: As a user with worktrees, I want to see which branch lives in which worktree.
Expected Behaviour (from code): In a multi-worktree repo, log annotates branches '(worktree: <path>[, dirty])'.

User Story: As a user, I want to know where I am in the stack.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st status' prints branch, status(role), parent, children, restack state, worktree clean/dirty.

User Story: As a user on an untracked branch, I want guidance.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Role 'untracked (run: st create or st track)'; parent '(untracked)'.

User Story: As a user mid-conflict, I want status to show the paused rebase.
Expected Behaviour (from code): During a rebase, reports 'rebase: in progress on X (run: st continue / st abort)' and conflicted files (JSON), even with detached HEAD.

User Story: As an agent, I want status as JSON.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st status --json' emits branch/trunk/role/parent/children/needsRestack/worktreeClean/rebase fields.

User Story: As a user, I want to switch to a tracked branch by name.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st checkout X' checks out X (trunk or tracked); prints 'switched to X'.

User Story: As a user, I want to list tracked branches when I omit the name.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st checkout' lists trunk + tracked branches sorted, current marked '*'.

User Story: As a user, I want a clear error for an unknown/untracked branch.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st checkout X' where X untracked errors 'X is not a tracked branch'.

User Story: As a user with worktrees, I want checkout to teleport to the branch's worktree.
Expected Behaviour (from code): If branch lives in another worktree, writes cd directive (shim) or prints 'run: cd <path>' (no shim).

User Story: As a user, I want to move up the stack toward my leaves.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st up' checks out the single child; prints 'switched to X'.

User Story: As a user, I want to climb multiple levels with 'st up n'.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st up 2' climbs two child links (stops at branch points).

User Story: As a user at the top, I want a clear notice.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st up' at a leaf prints 'already at the top of the stack' (or 'switched to X (top of stack)').

User Story: As a user at a branch point, I want to be asked which child.
Expected Behaviour (from code): At >1 children, lists them: 'multiple children of X; pick one and run st checkout <name>'.

User Story: As a user, I want a usage error for invalid step counts.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st up 0' or '-1' errors 'step count must be at least 1'; non-int errors 'invalid step count'.

User Story: As a user, I want to move down toward trunk.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st down' checks out the parent; prints 'switched to X'.

User Story: As a user, I want 'st down n' to descend up to n levels, stopping at trunk.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Walks parent links up to n times, stopping at trunk.

User Story: As a user already on trunk, I want a clear notice.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st down' on trunk prints 'already at trunk: X'.

User Story: As a user, I want to jump to the top of my current stack.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st top' walks single-children to the leaf and checks it out: 'moved to top of stack: X'.

User Story: As a user at a branch point, I want to be told to pick.
Expected Behaviour (from code): At >1 children errors 'X is a branch point with N children; use st checkout to pick one'.

User Story: As a user already at the top, I want a clear notice.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Prints 'already at the top of the stack: X'.

User Story: As a user, I want to jump to the bottom branch (just above trunk).
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st bottom' checks out the branch whose parent is the trunk: 'switched to bottom: X'.

User Story: As a user on trunk, I want a clear notice.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st bottom' on trunk prints 'at trunk'.

User Story: As a user already at the bottom, I want a clear notice.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Prints 'already at bottom: X'.

User Story: As a user, I want to fold my branch into its parent.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Parent advances to branch tip, branch deleted, children re-parented onto parent, descendants restacked: 'Folded X into Y'.

User Story: As a user, I want fold refused if the branch needs a restack.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Errors 'X needs restack before folding (run: st restack)'.

User Story: As a user, I want fold refused into the trunk.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Errors 'cannot fold X into the trunk Y'.

User Story: As a user on an untracked branch, I want fold refused.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Errors 'branch X is not tracked'.

User Story: As a user with a dirty tree, I want fold refused.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Returns ErrDirty (exit 4).

User Story: As a user, I want to squash all my branch's commits into one.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Squashes commits since parent into one (composed message of subjects), restacks descendants: 'Squashed N commits on X into one'.

User Story: As a user, I want to provide the squashed message with -m.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st squash -m msg' uses msg as the squashed commit message.

User Story: As a user with a single commit, I want a clear no-op.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Prints 'X already has a single commit; nothing to squash'.

User Story: As a user, I want squash refused if the branch needs a restack or tree is dirty.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Errors 'X needs restack before squashing' / ErrDirty on dirty tree.

User Story: As a user, I want to move my branch onto a new parent.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Re-parents current onto target, rebases it + descendants: 'Moved X onto Y'.
Errors Found: F4: text-mode rebase (onto/modify/restack/sync) leaks noisy git progress ("Rebasing (1/1)Successfully rebased...") before st's own summary. Add --quiet to the interactive rebase (keeps CONFLICT output).
Fix Applied: internal/git RebaseOnto passes --quiet: clean rebases (onto/modify/restack/sync) no longer leak git's "Rebasing.../Successfully rebased" progress; conflict output preserved.

User Story: As a user, I want a no-op if already on that parent.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Prints 'X is already stacked on Y'.

User Story: As a user, I want onto-itself rejected.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Errors 'cannot move X onto itself'.

User Story: As a user, I want onto a descendant rejected.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Errors 'cannot move X onto its own descendant Y'.

User Story: As a user, I want onto an invalid target rejected.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Errors 'target X is not the trunk or a tracked branch'.

User Story: As a user hitting a conflict mid-move, I want it recoverable.
Expected Behaviour (from code): On conflict records PendingReparent, returns ErrConflict (exit 2); 'st continue' promotes the new parent.

User Story: As a user, I want to delete a merged branch and re-parent its children.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Deletes branch, re-parents children onto its parent, restacks them: 'Deleted X; re-parented N branch(es) onto Y'.

User Story: As a user, I want deletion of an unmerged branch to require --force.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Errors 'branch X is not merged into its stack parent Y (use --force to delete anyway)'.

User Story: As a user, I want --force to delete regardless.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st delete X -f' deletes even if unmerged.

User Story: As a user, I want deletion of the trunk refused.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Errors 'cannot delete the trunk branch X'.

User Story: As a user, I want delete of an untracked branch refused.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Errors 'branch X is not tracked'.

User Story: As a user, I want to start tracking the current git branch (inferring its parent).
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st track' infers closest tracked ancestor (or trunk) as parent: 'Tracking X (parent: Y)'.

User Story: As a user, I want to set the parent explicitly with --parent.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st track --parent Y' tracks current with parent Y (must be trunk or tracked).

User Story: As a user, I want tracking the trunk refused.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Errors 'cannot track the trunk branch X'.

User Story: As a user, I want tracking an already-tracked branch refused.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Errors 'branch X is already tracked'.

User Story: As a user, I want an invalid --parent rejected.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Errors 'parent Y is not the trunk or a tracked branch'.

User Story: As a user, I want to stop tracking a branch but keep the git branch.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st untrack [name]' removes metadata, re-parents children onto parent (rewriting their base): 'Untracked X (re-parented children onto Y)'.

User Story: As a user, I want untracking the trunk refused.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Errors 'cannot untrack the trunk X'.

User Story: As a user, I want untracking an untracked branch refused.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Errors 'branch X is not tracked'.

User Story: As a user, I want to rename the current branch and update metadata.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st rename NEW' renames current branch, updates record + children pointers: 'Renamed OLD -> NEW'.
Errors Found: F3: "st rename <invalid-name>" leaks raw git "fatal: not a valid branch name" + hints. Validate up front.
Fix Applied: runRename validates newName via git.CheckBranchName; friendly "X is not a valid branch name".

User Story: As a user, I want to rename a specific branch by old+new.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st rename OLD NEW' renames OLD.

User Story: As a user, I want renaming the trunk to update the trunk metadata.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Renaming the trunk sets s.Trunk=NEW and re-points children.

User Story: As a user, I want a clear error renaming to an existing name or the same name.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Errors 'branch NEW already exists' / 'new name is the same as the old name'.

User Story: As a user, I want to fetch trunk, fast-forward it, prune merged branches, and restack.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st sync' fetches+FFs trunk, prunes merged, restacks all, restores branch: 'sync complete' + 'trunk: <ff result>'.
Errors Found: F6: "st sync --remote <missing>" silently reports success as "skipped (no remote)" (rc 0) instead of erroring like submit does. An explicitly-named missing remote should error.
Fix Applied: runSync now errors "remote X does not exist" when --remote is explicitly set to a missing remote (consistent with submit); a missing default origin still syncs locally.

User Story: As a user, I want to keep merged branches with --no-delete.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st sync --no-delete' does not prune merged branches.

User Story: As a user, I want to preview a sync with --dry-run.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st sync --dry-run' prints 'would delete'/'would restack', DryRun=true, mutates nothing; also requires clean tree.

User Story: As a user without a remote, I want sync to still restack locally.
Expected Behaviour (from code): No remote: 'trunk: skipped (no remote)', still prunes+restacks locally.

User Story: As a user with a dirty tree, I want sync refused.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Dirty tree returns ErrDirty (exit 4).

User Story: As a user, I want to push my whole stack to the remote without opening PRs.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st submit' pushes bottom..current with --force-with-lease, prints pushed list + 'open pull requests on your host: <URL>'.

User Story: As a user, I want to preview the pushes with --dry-run.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st submit --dry-run' prints 'would push X' per branch, pushes nothing.

User Story: As a user, I want to choose the remote with --remote.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st submit --remote NAME' pushes to NAME; errors 'remote NAME does not exist' if absent.

User Story: As a user on the trunk, I want a clear no-op.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st submit' on trunk prints 'at trunk; nothing to submit'.

User Story: As a user on an untracked branch, I want submit refused.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Errors 'branch X is not tracked by stacked'.

User Story: As a user, I want to resume a restack after resolving a conflict.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st continue' completes the in-progress rebase, records new base, restacks the rest: 'continued restack' + 'completed: X'.

User Story: As a user with no rebase in progress, I want a clear error.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Errors 'no rebase in progress; nothing to continue'.

User Story: As a user, I want to abort an in-progress restack and roll back.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st abort' runs git rebase --abort, clears pending reparent; already-restacked branches keep positions.

User Story: As a user with no rebase, I want a clear error.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Errors 'no rebase in progress; nothing to abort'.

User Story: As a user, I want abort to work even when stacked is uninitialized.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st abort' in an uninitialized repo still aborts the rebase (state nil).

User Story: As a user, I want to undo my last stack-mutating command.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st undo' rolls back metadata + resets recorded branch tips, working tree untouched: 'undid: <label>' + restored branches + git status note.

User Story: As a user with nothing to undo, I want a clear notice.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Prints 'nothing to undo'.

User Story: As a user mid-rebase, I want undo refused.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Errors 'cannot undo while a rebase is in progress; run st abort or resolve conflicts and run st continue'.

User Story: As a user, I want to check my stack for drift/inconsistencies.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st validate' on a clean stack prints 'ok: N tracked branch(es), no problems found', exit 0.

User Story: As a user, I want validate to flag problems and exit non-zero for scripts.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Lists problems (missing trunk/branch, bad parent, cycle), exits non-zero ('validate found N problem(s)').

User Story: As a user, I want drift surfaced as a warning (still exit 0).
Expected Behaviour (from code): Drifted-but-consistent branches listed under warnings, exit 0.

User Story: As a user, I want to auto-reconcile metadata with the repo.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st repair' untracks deleted branches, re-parents invalid/cyclic parents onto trunk, prints fixes + 'run st restack ...'.

User Story: As a user with a consistent stack, I want a clear no-op.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Prints 'nothing to repair; the stack is consistent with the repository'.

User Story: As a user, I want to materialize a branch's own worktree.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st worktree X' creates a worktree at ~/.stacked/worktrees/<repo>/<branch>, copies .worktreeinclude matches: 'created worktree: X -> <path>'.
Errors Found: F2: "st worktree <current-branch>" prints "worktree already exists -> <main repo path>", pointing at the main worktree as if a dedicated one exists (misleading).
Fix Applied: cmd worktreeAdd uses stack.LinkedOwnerOf + MainWorktree; current/main-worktree branch gets a clear "checked out in the main worktree (...); switch it to another branch first" message.

User Story: As a user, I want to list all worktrees.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st worktree ls' lists each worktree (branch/path; (bare)/(detached) labels).

User Story: As a user, I want to remove a branch's worktree.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st worktree rm X' removes the worktree: 'removed worktree X (<path>)'.
Errors Found: F1: rm of a branch that lives only in the MAIN worktree leaks raw "fatal: ... is a main working tree: exit status 128" (exit 1) instead of a friendly message.
Fix Applied: cmd worktreeRemove uses stack.LinkedOwnerOf; a branch only in the main worktree gets "checked out in the main worktree, not a separate one; nothing to remove" instead of git's raw "is a main working tree" fatal.

User Story: As a user re-materializing, I want an idempotent result.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st worktree X' when it exists prints 'worktree already exists' with the path.
Errors Found: F2: re-materializing the current/main-worktree branch reports "worktree already exists -> <main repo path>" (same root cause as US-105 F2).
Fix Applied: Same fix as US-105 (LinkedOwnerOf); re-materializing the current/main-worktree branch no longer claims a dedicated worktree "already exists".

User Story: As a user, I want clear errors for untracked branch / missing worktree / no arg.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Errors 'X is not a tracked branch' / 'X has no worktree' / 'worktree requires a branch name (or: ls, rm <branch>)'.

User Story: As a user, I want a shell shim that teleports my shell into a branch's worktree.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st shell install [bash|zsh|fish]' prints the shim function (auto-detects from $SHELL); used via eval.

User Story: As a user, I want a clear error for an unsupported shell.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st shell foo' errors 'unsupported shell foo (supported: bash, zsh, fish)'.

User Story: As a user, I want shell completion for st subcommands.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st completion <bash|zsh|fish>' prints a completion script generated from the live command registry.

User Story: As a user, I want a usage error for missing/unknown shell.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st completion' errors 'completion requires one shell argument: bash, zsh, or fish'; unknown shell errors too.

User Story: As a user/agent, I want the recommended workflow.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st guide' prints the workflow steps + exit-code summary + 'Use st help <command>'.

User Story: As a user, I want to list all commands.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st help' (or no args) prints command list with summaries + 'New here?' hint.

User Story: As a user, I want help for a single command.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st help <cmd>' prints summary, usage line, aliases.

User Story: As an agent, I want help as JSON.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st help --json' / 'st help <cmd> --json' emit command metadata incl. flags.

User Story: As a user, I want the version and build info.
Expected Behaviour (from code): 'st version' prints version + commit/built/go when available; '--json' emits the same.

User Story: As a user mistyping a command, I want a suggestion.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Unknown command errors 'unknown command X, did you mean Y? (run st help for usage)' (edit distance <=2).

User Story: As an agent, I want stable semantic exit codes.
Expected Behaviour (from code): Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 generic, 2 conflict, 3 not_initialized, 4 dirty, 70 internal panic; --json errors carry {code,message}.

User Story: As an agent, I want every command (except completion/shell) to accept --json.
Expected Behaviour (from code): All registered commands accept --json producing machine-readable output; completion/shell emit scripts only.

User Story: As a user in an uninitialized repo, I want a consistent not-initialized error.
Expected Behaviour (from code): State-reading/mutating commands error 'stacked is not initialized in this repo (run: st init)', exit 3.
